sentences.text: Good evening.
Before you check again, pray through tonight’s worries and place each concern in God’s care.
You may have checked the same message several times, hoping a reply would change how you feel.
You can put the phone within reach but turn its face away.
Let the place where you are sitting or lying support your weight.
You can arrive with a busy mind.
In this prayer, you will name your concerns separately, so you do not have to wrestle with every uncertainty at once.
Casting all your care upon him;
for he careth for you.
Father, I begin with the concern closest to the surface.
I give it a plain name before you.
It may be an unanswered message, a decision at work, or someone whose voice sounded troubled.
I have carried it through dinner and into this room.
Now I bring it into our conversation.
Help me entrust this particular care to you, even before my feelings catch up with the words I am praying.
When several worries arrive together, you can feel as though your whole life needs fixing before bedtime.
You can take a smaller approach here.
You are allowed to name one subject and let the others wait their turn.
You do not need a complete explanation.
A person’s name, a pending answer, or a sentence about tomorrow is enough to begin.
You are addressing someone who cares about the person doing the praying.
Lord, I bring the answer I cannot make arrive.
I have imagined reasons for the silence and measured the hours since I last checked.
Help me stop treating a missing reply as a verdict about my worth.
If there is a sensible time to follow up, let me choose it in daylight.
For this evening, receive both my hope and my disappointment.
Hold the uncertainty I cannot settle by checking again.
Father, help me make one kind boundary with the stream of information.
Let necessary messages remain available without making every notification my responsibility.
I ask for wisdom about the difference between being reachable and being constantly on watch.
If no urgent duty requires my attention, help me let the phone grow quiet.
I give you the impulse to search for one more update, and the fear that stopping means I have stopped caring.
Be careful for nothing;
but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
You hear an invitation to bring requests to God.
You can speak about what you need without first making yourself sound confident.
You can ask for an honest conversation, a workable plan, or help getting through an appointment.
Your request can be specific.
You can also remember a small kindness from today.
Gratitude gives another truth room beside the worry;
you do not have to pretend the worry has already disappeared.
Lord, I name the work concern that followed me home.
There is something I sent, something I missed, or something I may be asked to explain.
Help me separate the actual facts from the harsh story I am telling about myself.
If I made an error, give me the honesty to acknowledge it and the patience to correct it.
Tonight I hand over the imagined meeting that keeps starting again inside my head.
Father, make the next useful step clear enough to recognize.
Perhaps I need to check a number, ask a question, or explain a delay.
I do not need to rehearse every response another person might give.
Help me prepare what is mine to prepare and leave their reaction outside my control.
Receive my desire to do good work.
Let that desire become steady attention tomorrow, rather than another hour of self-punishment tonight.
God, I remember a moment today when someone made a difficult thing easier.
Perhaps they answered patiently, held a door, or let me start a sentence again.
Thank you for that ordinary generosity.
Thank you for the ability to ask for help and for people who have helped before.
I bring this memory alongside the unfinished work.
My day contained more than the moment I keep regretting;
help me remember it with greater honesty.
And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
You do not have to solve the meaning of every word tonight.
Notice that the promise speaks of hearts and minds, the very places where you may feel tired.
You can ask for God’s peace while there are unanswered questions around you.
You are not being asked to explain everything into order.
You can turn toward Christ with the thoughts you have, including the ones you wish would leave you alone.
Father, I name the household expense that has been pressing on me.
I bring the bill, the estimate, or the balance I need to review.
Give me clear judgment when I look at the facts.
Help me ask about arrangements when I need them, and speak honestly with anyone who shares this responsibility.
I place these practical concerns before you without inventing a certainty about how they will turn out.
Guide my next responsible choice.
Lord, I release the midnight calculations that repeat without giving me new information.
Tomorrow, help me set aside a definite time to look carefully, with paper, accurate figures, and whatever advice is needed.
Keep shame from isolating me.
Let courage take the form of a call made or a question asked.
Tonight I give you my fear of falling behind, and ask for companionship and wisdom as I address what is real.
You can pause before naming anything else.
Feel where your hands have come to rest.
You do not need to move them into a special position.
Let an ordinary breath come and go.
For these moments, you can leave the unfinished calculation unfinished.

for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself.

I bring the questions I hope to ask and the answers I am afraid to hear.
Help me bring any notes or documents I need, and seek appropriate support if I want someone with me.

As I leave the rest with you, teach me a love that respects their voice, their choices, and my own limits.

Help me resist filling that silence with accusations against myself or someone else.
Where I owe an apology, let it be sincere and specific.
Where I need clarification, help me ask kindly.

You can return as many times as you need, with less argument and more kindness.
Lord, when the same concern returns, help me answer it gently.
I have named it before you.
I have considered whether anything requires action now.
If there is no new information and no present responsibility, help me stop reopening the case.
Receive my repeated turning toward you.

because he trusteth in thee.

You can turn that way now.

Faithful God, I place my trust in your character rather than the strength of my concentration.
I know how easily my attention wanders.
Help me return to what is true about you with patience.
Keep me from using this prayer as another task to perform flawlessly.
I want to become more honest in your presence, more willing to receive help, and more able to leave an unanswered question without following it through every imagined outcome.
Father, I have named the unanswered message, the work concern, the practical expense, the coming appointment, and the person I love.
Receive whichever of these belongs to my life tonight.
Receive also the worry I could not explain aloud.
I do not need to make them one enormous burden again.
Each has been brought before you separately.
Help me remember that I can address one real responsibility at a time when morning comes.

You cannot determine a conversation’s outcome, but you can choose when to ask for one.

choose one concern that needs attention tomorrow, and give it one practical next step and a time.

You may find that you have fewer words now, or you may notice that your mind remains active.
Either way, you can let the prayer become simpler.
You have already said much that matters.
You do not need to repeat every concern to keep it within God’s attention.
You can rest beside a single truth from these readings, allowing the rest of the conversation to become quiet without bringing it to a perfect conclusion.
Father, I bring the urge to keep counting the hours.
Sometimes I turn the clock into another source of pressure, measuring how well I am resting.
Help me step away from that judgment.
Give me patience for the present moment, whether it is quiet or restless.
I ask for the rest I need without bargaining with the night.
Receive my wish for an easier morning, and help me meet whatever morning brings with appropriate support and care.
Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
The invitation begins with coming.
You can come with the weight you actually carry, even if you cannot explain why it feels so heavy.
You can come after a productive day or a day that seemed to get away from you.
You can come with faith that feels small.
You do not need to sort yourself into a more acceptable condition first.
Let the welcome of Jesus have room in the place where you are resting.
Jesus, I answer your welcome with the small amount of attention I have left.
I bring the weight of trying to be ready for every possibility.
Teach me a life that receives help and makes room for rest.
I leave the next step in its appointed place tomorrow.
For these remaining moments, let my prayer be uncomplicated:
I am here before you, with my weariness, trusting your invitation enough to stop preparing another explanation.
You can leave tonight unfinished in small, ordinary ways.
The note can stay folded.
The message can remain where you left it.
The question can wait for the person who can answer it.
You have not forgotten your responsibilities;
you have given one of them a practical place.
Now you can allow the night to contain something besides preparation.
You can listen, be still, and receive these moments without turning them into another assignment.
Father, I place this evening before you just as it has been.
Thank you for hearing each concern separately and receiving the words I struggled to find.
Help me carry the practical commitment into tomorrow when its time comes.
Until then, I ask for a gentle heart toward myself and those around me.
Let your care remain the thought beside my unanswered questions.
I leave the conversation here for now, held within your enduring love.
